name: Breast cancer (early stage)
theme: the operation is also a readout · pCR-adaptive therapy

meta.title: Early-stage breast cancer in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Early-stage invasive breast cancer (stages I-III), adult
meta.population: Adults with newly diagnosed invasive breast cancer, stages I-III - the most commonly diagnosed cancer in women, and the factory's first hormone-driven, biomarker-fragmented solid tumor. Three receptor-defined diseases share one anatomy: HR+/HER2- (where a printed genomic score decides chemotherapy), HER2+ (where the operation is also a readout - residual disease rewrites the plan), and triple-negative (where immunotherapy moved into the curative setting on a survival win). Male breast cancer and Paget disease are managed inside this pathway (variant notes); DCIS, metastatic disease, and inflammatory breast cancer exit to their own rows; phyllodes tumor is out of scope (not a carcinoma).
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the cancer where de-escalation has the strongest randomized pedigree in oncology (survival-equivalent lumpectomy, spared axillae, omitted radiation, chemotherapy withheld by a genomic score) and where the newest escalations must earn their rank the hard way: the monarchE card was PROMOTED this year (overall survival turned positive, Ann Oncol 2026) while the NATALEE card still displays a labeled disease-free endpoint and does not rank. The signature archetype is pCR-adaptive therapy - the operation is also a readout, and residual disease rewrites the p…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: AJCC 8th edition (anatomic + prognostic stage groups - still current for breast; v9 has not reached this site); ASCO/CAP receptor testing (ER/PR 2020, HER2 2018+2023 - binary HER2 reporting; HER2-low/ultralow is metastatic-row territory)
meta.response: Pathologic complete response (pCR) at surgery after neoadjuvant therapy - the readout that routes adjuvant therapy; RECIST plays no role in the curative setting

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: Median age at diagnosis is the early 60s. Age moves real forks: RT omission is randomized-backed at 65+, and the genomic-score interaction runs on menopause, not birthdays.
Patient.helpPatient: Plans flex with age - including proof that some parts of treatment can be safely skipped later in life.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: Most early breast cancer patients are fully active - fitness shapes chemotherapy intensity choices more than eligibility.
Patient.helpPatient: How much daily life is limited right now - usually not at all in early disease.

Patient.label: Menopausal status
Patient.help: The interaction the assay cannot see: RxPONDER found chemotherapy benefit in premenopausal node-positive patients even at scores <= 25 (5-yr IDFS 93.9% vs 89.0%) while postmenopausal patients gained…
Patient.helpPatient: Whether menopause has happened changes one important chemotherapy answer - the trainer shows exactly where.

Disease.label: Receptor subtype (ASCO/CAP ER/PR/HER2)
Disease.help: Three diseases share one anatomy, and every fork below is receptor-routed. HER2 reporting stays binary per ASCO/CAP 2023 - HER2-low/ultralow matters on the metastatic row, not here.
Disease.helpPatient: Three lab results sort this cancer into one of three quite different diseases - every plan decision follows from them.

Disease.label: Nodal status (pathologic)

Newly diagnosed.name: Endocrine therapy alone (TAILORx/RxPONDER - chemotherapy honestly withheld)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN Breast Cancer V4.2026 (per JNCCN listing; nccn.org 403 - secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the endocrine ledger: hot flashes, arthralgias, bone density (AIs), the adherence marathon - and no chemotherapy toxicity at all, by trial-grade permission
Newly diagnosed.patient: For hormone-driven cancer with a low genomic score: a daily tablet for years - and trial-grade proof that adding chemotherapy would not have helped.
drugs: Aromatase inhibitor or tamoxifen (+/- ovarian suppression per SOFT/TEXT risk)

Newly diagnosed.name: Chemotherapy + endocrine therapy (where the score - or premenopausal biology - earns it)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the chemotherapy season (alopecia, neuropathy, counts) followed by the endocrine decade; fertility preservation belongs BEFORE cycle one in young patients
Newly diagnosed.patient: Where the genomic score or biology says chemotherapy genuinely helps: a few months of it, then the hormone tablet years.

Newly diagnosed.name: Abemaciclib + endocrine therapy (monarchE - promoted this year: the OS is real)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN Breast Cancer V4.2026 (secondhand); FDA scope per 2023-03 expansion (date secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - IDFS met, OS now significant (2026)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: diarrhea (the class signature, front-loaded and manageable), fatigue, VTE vigilance - two years of it, traded for the survival margin
Newly diagnosed.patient: For higher-risk node-positive hormone-driven cancer: two years of a capsule added to the hormone tablet - and as of this year, proof it helps people live longer, not just relapse later.

Newly diagnosed.name: Ribociclib + endocrine therapy (NATALEE - the not-yet-promoted sibling)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - iDFS met; OS not yet significant
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: neutropenia and QT monitoring (the ribociclib signature), three years of it - a longer commitment than the promoted sibling, on younger evidence
Newly diagnosed.patient: The other capsule-plus-tablet option, open to a broader risk group - honest label: it keeps cancer from returning, and whether it lengthens life is still being answered.

Newly diagnosed.name: Paclitaxel + trastuzumab (APT - the small-tumor de-escalation standard)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: neuropathy (paclitaxel, usually mild at this exposure), cardiac surveillance on trastuzumab - the gentlest HER2 road
Newly diagnosed.patient: For small HER2-positive cancers without node spread: twelve gentle chemotherapy weeks plus a year of the antibody - with ten-year proof it is enough.

Newly diagnosed.name: Neoadjuvant HP-chemotherapy -> pCR-adaptive completion (the readout road)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized components (APHINITY, KATHERINE); TRAIN-2 for the anthracycline-free backbone
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the full HER2 season: chemotherapy months, dual-antibody infusions, cardiac surveillance - front-loaded so the pathology report can steer the rest
Newly diagnosed.patient: For larger or node-positive HER2-positive cancer: strong treatment first, then surgery that doubles as a test - what the pathologist finds honestly decides the second half of the plan.
drugs: Taxane/carboplatin + trastuzumab/pertuzumab -> surgery -> HP or T-DM1 by pCR

Newly diagnosed.name: Pembrolizumab + chemotherapy, neoadjuvant->adjuvant (KEYNOTE-522 - the TNBC survival win)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN Breast Cancer V4.2026 (secondhand); FDA 2021-07-26 (fda.gov-listed, flagged)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - pCR, EFS, and OS all met
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: chemotherapy's full season plus immune-related events (thyroid foremost, some permanent) - the honest price of the survival margin, stated on the card
Newly diagnosed.patient: For stage II-III triple-negative cancer: immunotherapy woven through the chemotherapy, before and after surgery - proven to help more people be alive at five years.

Newly diagnosed.name: Adjuvant olaparib (OlympiA - the germline result that becomes therapy)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - iDFS and OS met
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: nausea and fatigue early, anemia monitored - a gentle year by chemotherapy standards, with MDS/AML vigilance that the 6-year data keeps reassuring
Newly diagnosed.patient: For inherited-BRCA carriers with higher-risk disease: a year of a targeted tablet added after standard treatment - proven to help more people stay alive and cancer-free.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from therapy; local disease control becomes the eventual craft
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining treatment is a real choice - in this disease the road is measured in years, and the card shows honest numbers for both the road taken and the cure declined.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Complete excision + radiation where available (curative intent, again)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: standard of care (excision series; teaching estimate flagged)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the second operation and its field; systemic decisions ride the CALOR split
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A local return is still curable: remove it completely, add radiation where possible, and choose the drug question by the cancer's receptors.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Chemotherapy after excised recurrence (CALOR - the receptor-split answer)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized (small, n=162; effect concentrated ER-negative)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: a chemotherapy season, spent only where the receptors say it buys something
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: After removing a returned cancer, chemotherapy helps dramatically if the cancer is hormone-receptor-negative - and measurably not at all if it is hormone-driven. The card follows the evidence.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Choosing comfort with symptoms managed well - and if the cancer has spread further, the metastatic trainer holds that road's real (often long) numbers.

milestones.title: Subtype triple (HR/HER2) + stage extent before any plan
review: stage extent (DCIS routes out; inflammatory routes out; metastatic routes out)

milestones.title: Genomic assay before chemoendocrine commitment (HR+/HER2-)
review: menopausal status (it co-routes: RxPONDER's premenopausal split)

trials.name: OFSET / NRG-BR009: does chemo add anything to ovarian suppression + endocrine therapy? (premenopausal, RS <= 25)
DEBRA / NRG-BR007: radiation omission by genomic score (age 50-70, stage I, RS <= 18)
ATEMPT 2.0: T-DM1-based de-escalation for stage I HER2+ (the APT question, next generation)
OptimICE-pCR / Alliance A012103: after pCR, is adjuvant pembrolizumab still needed? (TNBC)
ASCENT-05 / OptimICE-RD: sacituzumab + pembrolizumab for residual TNBC (the other branch)
CAMBRIA-1: switch to camizestrant for extended adjuvant therapy (ER+, intermediate/high risk)
SCARLET / SWOG S2212: anthracycline-free chemoimmunotherapy for TNBC (shorter, kinder, same cure?)

refs.label: Allison et al. ER/PR testing in breast cancer: ASCO/CAP guideline update (incl. ER-low-positive 1-10% category). JCO 2020;38:1346-66

Wolff et al. HER2 testing ASCO/CAP: 2018 focused update + 2023 update (binary reporting reaffirmed; HER2-low not endorsed as a category - the low/ultralow story is metastatic-row territory). JCO 2023;41:3867-72

AJCC Cancer Staging, 8th edition (breast: anatomic + receptor-informed prognostic stage groups) - still current for breast; the v9 rollout has not reached this site (verify at each refresh; facs.org PDF unfetched this run)

Fisher et al. Twenty-year follow-up of NSABP B-06: lumpectomy + RT vs mastectomy - no survival difference (HR for death 0.97); RT cut in-breast recurrence 39.2% -> 14.3%. Twin proof: Veronesi 20-yr (Milan), same conclusion. NEJM 2002;347:1233-41
EBCTCG meta-analysis: RT after BCS - 10-yr recurrence 35.0% -> 19.3%, 15-yr breast-cancer death 25.2% -> 21.4%; one death avoided per four recurrences avoided. Lancet 2011;378:1707-16
Giuliano et al. ACOSOG Z0011 10-yr: sentinel-node dissection alone vs ALND (1-2 positive nodes, BCS+RT) - 10-yr OS 86.3% vs 83.6%, noninferior; the trial that spared the axilla. JAMA 2017;318:918-26

Kunkler et al. PRIME II (age >=65, low-risk HR+, endocrine-treated): RT omission - 10-yr local recurrence 9.5% vs 0.9%, 10-yr OS identical (80.8% vs 80.7%), distant recurrence not increased. NEJM 2023;388:585-94

Haviland et al. START trials 10-yr: hypofractionated whole-breast RT (40 Gy/15) - locoregional relapse 4.3% vs 5.5% with less late toxicity; FAST-Forward later shrank it to one week. Lancet Oncol 2013;14:1086-94 (PMID 24055415 - a circulating wrong PMID for this paper resolves to a child-psychology article; corrected this run)

Sparano et al. TAILORx (RS 11-25, node-negative HR+/HER2-): endocrine alone noninferior to chemoendocrine - 9-yr IDFS 83.3% vs 84.3%, 9-yr OS 93.9% vs 93.8%; RSxage interaction (some chemo benefit <=50 with RS 16-25). 12-yr cut is SABCS-2022 congress-level (late recurrences now exceed early - flagged). NEJM 2018;379:111-21

Kalinsky et al. RxPONDER (1-3 nodes, RS <=25): postmenopausal - NO chemo benefit (5-yr IDFS 91.9% vs 91.3%); premenopausal - real benefit (93.9% vs 89.0%, HR 0.60) - the menopausal interaction the menu encodes. NEJM 2021;385:2336-47
Piccart et al. MINDACT 8.7-yr (70-gene signature): clinical-high/genomic-low without chemo - 5-yr DMFS 94.7%; the other assay road to chemo omission. Lancet Oncol 2021;22:476-88
EBCTCG: 5 years of tamoxifen in ER+ disease - recurrence RR 0.53 (years 0-4), breast-cancer mortality reduced ~a third through 15 years. Lancet 2011;378:771-84
EBCTCG: aromatase inhibitors vs tamoxifen - ~30% proportional recurrence reduction while treatments differ; 10-yr breast-cancer mortality 12.1% vs 14.2%. Lancet 2015;386:1341-52

Francis/Pagani et al. SOFT 12-yr + SOFT/TEXT 13-yr (JCO 2023 x2 - not NEJM, corrected this run): ovarian suppression added to tamoxifen improves outcomes with OS trend (12-yr OS 89.0% vs 86.8%, HR 0.78); exemestane+OFS adds DFS (Delta 4.6%) with OS gains concentrated in higher-risk subgroups. JCO 2023;41:1370 & 1376
Rastogi et al. monarchE 5-yr (JCO 2024): IDFS HR 0.680, absolute Delta 7.6% (5-yr rates 83.6% vs 76.0%); OS not significant at that interim - the card's labeled years. JCO 2024;42:987-93

Johnston et al. monarchE overall survival (Ann Oncol 2026, online 2025-10): OS HR 0.842 (0.722-0.981, p=0.027) - boundary MET; 7-yr OS 86.8% vs 85.0%, 7-yr iDFS 77.4% vs 70.9%; fewer patients alive with metastatic disease. THE PROMOTION: the labeled card became a ranked card. Ann Oncol 2026;37:155
Fasching et al. NATALEE 4-yr (JAMA Oncol 2025): iDFS 88.5% vs 83.6% (HR 0.72); OS immature (HR 0.83). JAMA Oncol 2025

Hortobagyi et al. NATALEE final iDFS analysis: 3-yr iDFS 90.7% vs 87.6% (HR 0.749, p=0.0012; node-negative subgroup benefit included); 5-yr analysis (ESMO Open 2025): iDFS HR 0.716, OS STILL not significant (HR 0.800, 0.637-1.003). Ann Oncol 2024

Tolaney et al. APT 10-yr final (Lancet Oncol 2023): paclitaxel + trastuzumab for <=3 cm node-negative HER2+ - 10-yr iDFS 91.3%, OS 94.3%, breast-cancer-specific survival 98.8% (7-yr DFS was 93%, JCO 2019 - the two figures are different timepoints, kept straight this run). Lancet Oncol 2023;24:273-85

Geyer et al. KATHERINE survival analysis (NEJM 2025): T-DM1 for residual HER2+ disease after neoadjuvant therapy - 7-yr iDFS 80.8% vs 67.1% (Delta 13.7), OS HR 0.66 (p=0.003), 7-yr OS 89.1% vs 84.4%. The rewrite branch's survival proof. NEJM 2025;392 (online 2025-01-16)

Loibl et al. APHINITY 8.4-yr (JCO 2024): 8-yr OS 92.7% vs 92.0% (HR 0.83, p=0.078 at that interim); node-positive 8-yr iDFS 86.1% vs 81.2%. CODA (flagged, congress-level): the 11.3-yr final analysis (ESMO Breast 2025) reports OS significance - HR 0.83, p=0.044, node-positive-concentrated - confirm at publication. JCO 2024;42:3643

van Ramshorst et al. TRAIN-2: neoadjuvant carboplatin/taxane + HP - pCR 68% WITHOUT anthracyclines vs 67% with (and 3-yr EFS equal): anthracyclines added toxicity, not efficacy. The honest pCR anchor for the HP era. Lancet Oncol 2018;19:1630-40
Schmid et al. KEYNOTE-522 (stage II-III TNBC): neoadjuvant pembrolizumab + chemo - pCR 64.8% vs 51.2%; 36-mo EFS 84.5% vs 76.8% (HR 0.63). NEJM 2020;382:810-21

Schmid et al. KEYNOTE-522 overall survival (NEJM 2024): 5-yr OS 86.6% vs 81.7% (p=0.002; HR 0.66) - immunotherapy in the curative TNBC setting, earned on survival; 5-yr EFS 81.3% vs 72.3% (63-mo cut). NEJM 2024;391:1981-91

Masuda et al. CREATE-X: adjuvant capecitabine for residual HER2- disease after neoadjuvant chemo - TNBC subset 5-yr DFS 69.8% vs 56.1%, OS 78.8% vs 70.3% (HR 0.52). Registry: UMIN000000843 (no NCT exists - Japanese registry). NEJM 2017;376:2147-59
Tutt et al. OlympiA (germline BRCA1/2, high-risk HER2-): adjuvant olaparib x1 yr - 3-yr iDFS 85.9% vs 77.1% (HR 0.58). NEJM 2021;384:2394-405

Geyer et al. OlympiA OS (Ann Oncol 2022): 4-yr OS 89.8% vs 86.4% (HR 0.68, p=0.009); 6.1-yr cut (SABCS 2024, congress-level, flagged): 6-yr iDFS 79.6% vs 70.3%, OS HR 0.72, no excess MDS/AML. Ann Oncol 2022;33:1250-68
Aebi et al. CALOR: chemotherapy after excised isolated locoregional recurrence - 5-yr DFS 69% vs 57% (HR 0.59), interaction favoring ER-negative. Lancet Oncol 2014;15:156-63

Wapnir et al. CALOR final (9-yr median follow-up): benefit ENTIRELY in ER-negative recurrence - 10-yr DFS 70% vs 34% (HR 0.29); ER-positive HR 1.07 (nothing) - the cleanest receptor-split answer in the recurrence literature. JCO 2018;36:1073-9
EBCTCG: adjuvant bisphosphonates - breast-cancer mortality RR 0.82 in postmenopausal women (2p=0.002); no effect premenopausal. Lancet 2015;386:1353-61

Bedrosian et al. ASCO-SSO germline testing guideline (2024): offer BRCA1/2 testing to ALL newly diagnosed breast cancer <=65, and older with indications - the scope that unlocks OlympiA. JCO 2024;42:584-604

lidERA (giredestrant adjuvant, SABCS 2025, congress-level): first positive adjuvant SERD - iDFS HR 0.70, 3-yr iDFS 92.4% vs 89.6%; FDA priority review with decision expected ~2026-11 - NOT approved as of 2026-08 (sponsor announcements; flagged)

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.
